title: Isolate anonymous feedback by signed session identity
description:
Problem: unauthenticated requests can share a common anonymous principal, allowing one visitor to overwrite or affect another visitor's per-turn feedback when only the shared principal is used as the feedback key.

Desired outcome: feedback ownership is isolated per signed session while preserving deliberate authenticated-user behavior.

Scope:
- Issue a cryptographically signed, expiring anonymous session subject.
- Bind feedback reads, writes, and replacement operations to that subject plus the chat turn/session.
- Reject missing, expired, malformed, or replayed subjects without falling back to a global anonymous identity.
- Preserve retention and deletion behavior for anonymous records.
- Out of scope: full anonymous account creation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Two anonymous browser sessions cannot overwrite or read one another's feedback.
- Refresh within the configured session lifetime preserves the same visitor's own feedback behavior.
- Subject tampering and expiry are rejected.
- Authenticated users retain stable user-scoped feedback semantics.
- Regression tests cover concurrent anonymous sessions and cross-session access attempts.

Validation:
- Run focused chat feedback and authorization tests.
- Inspect persistence keys for absence of a global anonymous bucket.
- Run Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.
